exact_value.text: **FAQ p10:** An opponent flare prevented by Anti-Matter remains in hand, does not spend that player's flare limit, but cannot be attempted again that encounter. Anti-Matter Super must be played anew in each encounter in which its effect is wanted.

exact_value.heading: Actions / Flare system
exact_value.text: Return a flare to hand **immediately after its effect finishes**, rather than discard it, unless its effect states otherwise. A player may play **at most one flare per encounter**, and an individual flare can be used **only once per encounter even if it changes hands**. A Card Zap targeting the flare counts against the player's limit. Prevention of play differs from cancellation after play: see Anti-Matter's FAQ exception. If a Super enables a power use, that power can still be Cosmic Zapped even outside its usual role/phase. The flare remains in hand rather than being discarded or forced to Wild; Only Wild is available for an otherwise legal play while the power is zapped. Zapping the enabled power does not undo the already-played flare or permit a second play of it in the same encounter; the ordinary per-player and per-flare limits still apply. When your own Wild would otherwise be handed to your alien, keep it after resolution.

exact_value.heading: Flare system
exact_value.quote:
### Flare system

Flares are not encounter cards. Each has printed Wild and Super effects, usage roles and timing. Normally use Wild; if it is your own alien's flare and your power is available, **you must use Super**, not choose Wild. If your power is lost or zapped, you can use only Wild until your power returns.

Return a flare to hand **immediately after its effect finishes**, rather than discard it, unless its effect states otherwise. evidence.heading: Start Turn and hand replacement
evidence.quote:
### Start Turn and hand replacement

Start Turn occurs only before the first encounter of your turn, before Regroup effects. If offense has no encounter cards, reveal and discard the remaining hand, then draw eight new cards. You may first play legally playable non-encounter cards but are not required to play them. Hate draws a needed starting hand before using its power.

At Planning, a defense lacking encounter cards reveals/discards the remainder and draws eight cards, repeating until it has an encounter card. An offense that runs out later in its turn **when it needs to play an encounter card** ends its turn instead of drawing a replacement. Offense returns its committed ships to its own colonies; each ally returns that ally's committed ships to that ally's own colonies. The normal no-colony relocation rule applies. There is no automatic draw at the end of an encounter or turn, or merely for running out of cards. Alien and card effects can grant different draws.
